own_solution.law: For capacitor charging, V_C(t) = E[1 - exp(-t/(RC))]. Here RC = 0.100 s, so V_C(0.080 s) = 12[1 - exp(-0.8)].
assumptions: The battery, resistor and capacitor are ideal, with negligible capacitor leakage and battery internal resistance.
Each added series resistor is present from the initial connection.
Disconnecting the battery or opening the switch interrupts the charging loop without introducing a discharge path; the capacitor subsequently retains its voltage.

notes: The four resistor sentences consistently specify 2 kΩ. Disconnected resistors have no physical path to the target. Either added series-resistor sentence gives total resistance 7 kΩ and time constant 0.140 s. Both interruption sentences consistently specify 50 ms: charging stops at that time, giving V_C = 12[1 - exp(-0.5)] V, which persists until 80 ms under the ideal-capacitor assumption. T5388 is naturally read as adding a resistor to the already specified circuit.
